top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) are an original invention: magic-wavelength trapping with Lamb-Dicke confinement removes Doppler, recoil and differential light shifts while interrogating very many atoms, which neither the frequency comb nor single-ion control provides. The idea has been verified by independent laboratories intercomparing clocks at the 10^-18 level and it opens doors such as relativistic geodesy and tests of constant variation. The two-name allocation is compact, and the citation can be scoped to invention and realization; the remaining caveat is priority among early contributors, which an expert check should settle. Topological insulators come second because theory and the first HgTe experiment are cleanly attributable, IceCube third because the flux discovery is real but the three-name allocation and the confirmation of individual sources remain open, and no award last because a mature, verified discovery is available.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; as an electron microscopist I note a loose field affinity to aberration-corrected electron optics (B019), which is not on this slate, and a Chalmers colleague (Johansson) sits on the committee
